edit: on jitsi i now received explanation on services not necessarily supporting specific notification protocols, so now this makes sense to me

review_comments.body: could potentially assign a value to `reloadCommand` conditional on `reloadSignal != null`... something like `"${pkgs.coreutils}/bin/kill -${reloadSignal} $MAINPID`

```suggestion
      assertion = (config.process.reloadSignal && config.process.reloadCommand);
```

typo missing r
`kill` accepts `HUP` as a signal, not `SIGHUP` IIRC
this option should not impact notification protocol
maybe set to `null` here and then in `config` you can `mkIf` + `mkForce` to enforce the value?
maybe we can add an additional detail to be clear... command the underlying service manager will use to reload this daemon or some such... 🤔
`nix`lang has no implicit cast to bool as far as i know

let's expand this to include a few more details

something more along the lines of notification protocol this daemon supports for communication with the underlying service manager
this should be optional

unfortunately we cannot infer this ... we would need a separate option to store this... let's keep it simple logic for now and say `"notify"` instead of `"notify-reload"` and give this some more thought... 🤔

To address @KiaraGrouwstra's concern, we could remove `"s6"` and move the declaration of `"systemd"` being valid to the systemd module.

An s6 integration can similarly extend the enum on its own using type merging

This also could be a empty enum list so it's extensible, then a service could `["systemd", "s6"]` or `[ ]` if service supports none. Then check in service.nix in nixos if it contains systemd then do notify.

Although that would make it annoying to specify portable modules. If the service supports both protocols, it would needs conditionals on both just to stop offending the `enum` type check when loaded into a service manager that is unaware of the other.
`mkIf` + `mkForce`

at the risk of being rude by commenting post-approve (if not post-merge) still, my nit here would be we should probably make this a sub-module of boolean options for correctness (duplicates here would not make sense) to prevent people having to change their config to accommodate such a change later.

Again like this was discussed by @aanderse, It could be mentioned in the future. 
But for now there is no need to have a sub-module of boolean options, unless there is specific setting to readiness notification protocols which I assume from my research, there is not, hence it doesn't really need a sub-module. 

We already have in apply to make it unique so in the case of duplicates it doesn't matter, but however in upstream nixpkgs reviews as @aanderse said, we should encourage the user to not make duplicates in the notificationProtocol setting.

i agree with @KiaraGrouwstra in that we should aim for this - i just didn't want to hold up progress. 

i think @roberth said he had some thoughts about this

constraining irrelevant degrees of freedom i think has relevance outside UI generation as well - aside from constraining duplication here, it would also make it invariant to the order that such items might be specified in. that aside, having separate options for the various options may help document them or separately set defaults for them as well.

the list of enum form, on the other hand, i think mostly has brevity of configuration going for it.
this scalar string no longer matches its actual type
fixed in #540857
